$comment: ADR-037 register fragment (connectors-job-board-multiposting). The dormant LinkedIn job posting template and its mapping from humaniq's Vacancy, as one batch-create element of LinkedIn's simpleJobPostings call. No code: the openconnector.source-call and openconnector.apply-mapping flow nodes do the work, picked per board through a templated reference (jobboard-{{ json.channel }}).

objects.name: LinkedIn job postings
objects.description: LinkedIn's job posting API for partners (POST /v2/simpleJobPostings with X-Restli-Method: batch_create). Posting through it needs acceptance into LinkedIn's Talent Solutions partner programme (Job Posting API): apply there first, then set the OAuth client of the accepted application, the credential and the organisation URN on the mapping, and enable. The answer is a posting task per element (its id is the task URN), which the humaniq flow records as the posting's reference.

objects.name: humaniq Vacancy to a LinkedIn job posting
objects.description: One humaniq Vacancy (as the Vacature plaatsen flow passes it, one item per board, with vacancyId and channel) as the body of a LinkedIn simpleJobPostings batch create with one element. Before enabling, fill `elements.0.integrationContext` with your organisation URN (urn:li:organization:<id>) and `elements.0.companyApplyUrl` with the address candidates apply on, for example https://werken.example.nl/vacatures/{{ vacancyId }}. `listedAt` is the publication date in epoch milliseconds; the vacancy id is the external job posting id. The vacancy carries no place or contract type, so the location is the country and the employment status full time.
